questions: Did your walking problem begin gradually over months or years rather than suddenly?
Did it begin after starting or increasing a medication such as an antipsychotic, metoclopramide, or prochlorperazine?
Do you have stiffness or slowness in your arms or legs?
Do you have a tremor when a limb is relaxed?
Is one side of your body noticeably more affected than the other?
Have you noticed smaller handwriting, a softer voice, or reduced facial expression?
Do you ever feel that your feet are stuck to the floor when starting or turning?
Have you had falls or near-falls because of your walking?
Have you previously had a stroke or other sudden neurological event?
Have you had a significant head injury before these symptoms began?
Do you have weakness, numbness, or loss of coordination in an arm or leg?
Do you feel dizzy or faint when standing up?
Have you developed urinary urgency, urinary incontinence, or difficulty emptying your bladder?
Have you had constipation that began around the same time as the walking problem?
Have you lost your sense of smell?
Do you act out your dreams or move violently while asleep?
Have you experienced visual hallucinations while awake?
Have you noticed significant problems with memory, attention, or thinking?
Have you had double vision or difficulty looking up or down?
Have you become unusually sleepy during the day?
Have you had unexplained weight loss, trouble swallowing, or choking?
Do close relatives have Parkinson’s disease or a similar movement disorder?
